note: Informational record of the bug CATEGORIES the hidden oracle (oracle_test.ts, written transiently by grader.py) checks for. The builder writes createFsrsExportPayload() from scratch -- nothing is literally injected into its code. 'Seeded' here means 'plausible implementation mistakes a cheap builder model might make against this exact spec', which is what the oracle is designed to catch independent of whatever the spec-writer's own acceptance tests happened to cover.

bugs.description: Calls Date.now() or new Date() internally for exportedAt instead of using the passed `now` parameter, making the output non-deterministic and untestable against an explicit timestamp.
Computes rowCounts from the wrong array (e.g. auditLog count copied from events.length) or after some transformation (e.g. after deduping), instead of the original input arrays' raw lengths.

Returns the caller's original arrays/objects directly (payload.state === state, or payload.state[i] === state[i]) instead of a deep-enough copy -- mutating the original array or a row object after the call corrupts the already-returned 'export snapshot'.
Sorts or otherwise mutates the original state/events/auditLog arrays in place while building the payload (e.g. state.sort(...) instead of [...state].sort(...)).

Runs the rows through a Set/Map-based dedup step (e.g. by JSON.stringify-ing each row to a key), wrongly collapsing a legitimately-duplicated row object that appeared twice in the input into a single entry in the output.
Returns schemaVersion as the number 1 instead of the literal string "1" specified in the interface, or computes it dynamically instead of a fixed constant.
